This — and the elevation of WSH’s receivers in the Blough scheme via shifts and motions — gives me hope that their room might be more satisfactory than people think. 2) You see more man coverage on third down and in the red area. This makes early down success more important for a team like the Commanders. It also puts more pressure on Daniels to be awesome in the red zone to uplift those guys. 3) If it’s fair to say that McLaurin is the only guy who will routinely beat man coverage, Daniels being on the field is vital in helping to hide that issue. It’s tougher to run man vs a team with a QB who runs a 4.4.

title: Mental Health Check-In for today… Sorry I fell off from doing these for a while gang but I’m back to walk this walk together with you. People often ask me what’s something I do when I am REALLLLLY struggling, stuck in the gray what’s the best weapon I use to fight back. Power of connection! I call 2 people and tell them I’m struggling. I completely open up to them, am very vulnerable and tell them how bad it is between my ears. That’s my way of leaning into my TEAMMATES! I talk a lot about the power of TEAM. But then, just as important, I call 2 other people and don’t tell them I’m struggling but instead I just check up on THEM!! That’s my way of “Being Of Service” - another huge tool or pillar of mine I can use to fight back. By being of service it’s my way of fighting back my terrible self talk. When you make those last two calls, they always appreciate you caring. While 80 even 90 percent of the time they say they are fine… that other 10 percent, it is powerful!! That 10 percent often says that call came at the right time. They needed a call like that. One particular call, a few weeks later, my friend told me, “Remember when you called me to check up on me? Well, you don’t know this, but you saved my life that day. I wasn’t thinking right and I was planning on taking my life. That call saved me!” WOWWWW!!! Lean into your teammates gang!!! We all gotta build one big badass team together to fight back. Love yall #mentalhealth #mentalhealthmatters #depression #anxiety #team

title: The Washington Commanders announced today the team's 2026 Bill Walsh NFL Diversity Coaching Fellows for training camp: Ryan Crawford, Sammy Morris, and DJ Gillins. Washington will host all three fellows through the first week of the preseason schedule. Ryan Crawford will work with the defensive backs and is currently the associate head coach at Harvard University. Sammy Morris will assist the offensive line and special teams units and is currently the assistant director of player development and NFL liaison for Texas Tech University. DJ Gillins will work with the tight ends and offensive line and is joining Washington after his stint as a Bill Bidwill fellow and assistant tight ends coach for the Arizona Cardinals.

title: Nick Saban to @PatMcAfeeShow: "I think [the Big Ten over SEC] is a little bit of a cultural thing right now in college football. The SEC has enjoyed the fact that the Southeast plays great high school football. The high school is still the center of the community. Kids love to play. There's a lot of good players. They all used to grow up wanting to go to Alabama, Georgia or Florida or Texas A&M or Texas, or wherever. Now they're going all over the country because the culture allows them to do that. "I don't think that's a bad thing. But I do think that's helped some other conferences get a little better and they were already damned good. I have a lot of respect for the Big Ten. I coached in the Big Ten for 12 years. But the SEC is a pretty damn good league, too. If you look at the top [20] most difficult schedules, all 16 SEC teams are in the top [20] and nine of the top 10."

title: Tepper Sports & Entertainment and the Carolina Panthers have released new renderings of the Bank of America Stadium renovation project. This is in conjunction with announcing a long-term extension of their naming rights partner Bank of America and a significant additional private investment from owner David Tepper to the renovation. The initial upfront cost is now expected to be north of $1.3B — which includes the addition of new fan gathering spaces, a 500-level social patio and a 4,400 seat entertainment venue. The phased project is on track to be fully completed in 2030.
